newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares creep higher but investors nervous.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares creep higher but investors nervous.

text.p: Norwegian stocks continued to creep higher on Thursday with interest focused on blue chips due to uncertainty over U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
Concerns over domestic inflation ahead of next week's 1997 budget would continue to keep the market edgy, they said.

"The Fed Reserve's decision not to raise interest rates has only moved the unceratinty into the future until its next meeting," said one broker. "It would have been much better if they had acted last Tuesday."
Oslo's Total share climbed 0.46 percent to 845.16 points in a healthy turnover of almost 744 million crowns.

Brokers said profit taking was likely to creep into the banking sector following recent gains on lower interest rates. Norway's largest commercial bank Den norske Bank closed 0.10 crowns down at 20.50 crowns, while the second largest Christiania og Kreditkasse gained 0.20 crowns to 16.40 crowns.
But the recent takeover bid of Zurich Insurance for Norwegian group Protector was seen as a double edge sword for UNI Storebrand.
Dealers said Zurich's high offer for Protector showed confidence in the Norwegian market, but the merger would create stiff competition for UNI, Norway's largest life insurer.
